title: Footnotes Gone Feral
blurb: The parts of history your textbook skipped because nobody would believe them.

cards.say: Martin Van Buren [was the first president born after the Declaration of Independence], [gave us the word OK, which started out as his nickname], [grew up speaking Dutch as his first language], and [was the last sitting vice president elected president until 1988].
cards.real: OK first appeared in an 1839 Boston newspaper as a joke for oll korrect. His 1840 campaign's OK Clubs, for Old Kinderhook, made it popular.
src: https://www.history.com/news/who-was-the-first-president-born-an-american-citizen (born 1782; the seven presidents before him were all born before 1776)
https://www.merriam-webster.com/wordplay/the-hilarious-history-of-ok-okay (1839 Boston Morning Post, oll korrect; the 1840 OK Clubs only popularized it)
https://www.history.com/news/who-was-the-first-president-born-an-american-citizen (spoke Dutch as his first language)
https://www.history.com/news/who-was-the-first-president-born-an-american-citizen (the last sitting VP to win until George H.W. Bush in 1988)

cards.say: James Garfield [gave part of a campaign speech in German], [worked the mules on a canal boat as a teenager], [won his party's nomination on the 36th ballot], and [published his own proof of the Pythagorean theorem while president].
cards.real: His trapezoid proof was published in 1876, while he was a congressman from Ohio, five years before he became president.
src: https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/1880-front-porch-campaign-speeches.htm (October 16, 1880: addressed German immigrants in part in their native language)
https://wikiwand.com/en/James_A._Garfield (at 16, a canal boat job managing the mules that pulled it)
https://wikiwand.com/en/James_A._Garfield (compromise nominee on the 36th ballot)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garfield%27s_proof_of_the_Pythagorean_theorem; https://wikiwand.com/en/James_A._Garfield (published 1876, as a congressman)

cards.say: Chester A. Arthur [was born in Canada and moved to Vermont as a baby], [had Louis Comfort Tiffany's design firm redo rooms in the White House], [helped win a case that desegregated a New York streetcar line], and [sold 24 wagonloads of White House furniture at auction].
cards.real: Arthur was born in Vermont. The story that he was secretly born in Canada was a rumor that never held up.
src: https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/28917/21-things-you-didnt-know-about-21st-president (born in Vermont despite rumors he was born in Canada)
https://www.whitehousehistory.org/white-house-decorative-arts-in-the-1880s (Arthur commissioned Associated Artists, of which Louis Comfort Tiffany was a partner, to make over several rooms)

https://history.nycourts.gov/elizabeth-jennings-streetcar-desegregation-in-nyc/ (the case was assigned to junior partner Arthur; the jury found for Jennings and the Third Avenue Railroad agreed to desegregate its streetcars at once); https://millercenter.org/node/38820
https://www.whitehousehistory.org/white-house-decorative-arts-in-the-1880s (twenty-four wagonloads of furniture sent to auction)

cards.say: Grover Cleveland [got married inside the White House], [had secret surgery in a chair tied to the mast of a friend's yacht], [was mayor of New York City before becoming president], and [vetoed more bills in his first term than all earlier presidents combined].
cards.real: Cleveland was mayor of Buffalo in 1882 and then governor of New York, before winning the presidency in 1884.
src: https://millercenter.org/node/237 (married Frances Folsom in 1886, the first president married in the White House)
https://millercenter.org/node/237 (June 1893, aboard a friend's yacht, seated in a chair tied to the mast)
https://potus.com/grover-cleveland (mayor of Buffalo 1882, governor of New York 1883 to 1885)
https://potus.com/grover-cleveland (414 vetoes in his first term, more than double the 204 by all earlier presidents)

cards.say: Rutherford B. Hayes [got America's first Siamese cat as a gift from the King of Siam], [had the first White House telephone, and its number was 1], [took his first oath of office privately inside the White House], and [started the White House Easter Egg Roll after Congress banned it at the Capitol].
cards.real: Siam the cat came in 1878 from David Sickels, an American diplomat at the consulate in Bangkok, not from the king.
src: https://carlanthonyonline.com/2013/10/09/the-foreign-feline-of-president-hayes-first-siamese-cat-in-the-u-s/ (sent in 1878 by David Sickels, a US diplomat at the consulate in Bangkok)
https://mentalfloss.com/article/77785/first-oval-office-phone-wasnt-installed-until-1929 (installed 1877, phone number 1); https://historynet.com/?p=13689414
https://artsandculture.google.com/exhibit/rutherford-b-hayes/gQL40xJL (oath taken privately in the Red Room because March 4 fell on a Sunday)
https://thereconstructionera.com/?p=22536 (Congress outlawed the egg roll at the Capitol by 1876; Hayes opened the White House grounds in 1878)

cards.say: Dwight D. Eisenhower [was named David Dwight at birth], [was born in a small town in Kansas], [was kept home training troops in World War I despite asking to go overseas], and [got squirrels banished for digging up his White House putting green].
cards.real: Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas, in 1890. His family moved back to Kansas before he was two, and that's where he grew up.
src: https://www.history.com/articles/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-dwight-d-eisenhower (birth name David Dwight Eisenhower)
https://thc.texas.gov/state-historic-sites/eisenhower-birthplace/eisenhower-birthplace-history (born in Denison, Texas, October 14, 1890; back to Kansas at about 18 months)
https://www.history.com/articles/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-dwight-d-eisenhower (asked for an overseas assignment in World War I but stayed in training roles at home)
https://www.history.com/articles/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-dwight-d-eisenhower (1954 putting green; squirrels trapped and released in Rock Creek Park)

cards.say: Emperor Norton [demanded a bridge across San Francisco Bay decades before one was built], [paid for meals with money he issued himself], [pardoned the officer who arrested him], and [later added Protector of Canada to his royal title].
cards.real: His add-on title was Protector of Mexico, taken up in the 1860s. He had declared himself Emperor of the United States in 1859.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Norton (bridge decrees of 1872; the Bay Bridge opened in 1936)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Norton (his own scrip, 50 cents to 10 dollars, accepted by some restaurants)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Norton (1867: granted an Imperial Pardon to Armand Barbier, the officer who arrested him)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Norton (Emperor from September 17, 1859; Protector of Mexico by early 1866)

cards.say: Arthur Conan Doyle [believed two girls' fake fairy photos were real], [worked as a ship's surgeon on an Arctic whaling voyage], [was knighted for creating Sherlock Holmes], and [helped make skiing popular in Switzerland].
cards.real: Doyle was knighted in 1902 for his writing defending Britain's side in the Boer War, not for Sherlock Holmes.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottingley_Fairies
https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/sir-arthur-conan-doyle-went-on-his-own-adventuresto-the-arctic-52100539/ (ship's surgeon on the whaler Hope at 20, in 1880)
https://arthurconandoyle.co.uk/knight (knighted October 24, 1902, for his defense of Britain's cause in the Boer War)
https://swissinfo.ch/eng/culture/sherlock-holmes-creator-s-swiss-skiing-legacy-fact-or-fiction/49100300 (learned to ski in Davos in 1894 and helped popularise it, though he did not introduce it)

cards.say: Julia Child [was turned away by the Army for being too tall], [published her first cookbook at 39], [helped cook up a shark repellent for a US spy agency], and [voiced a character in a 1993 animated dinosaur movie].
cards.real: Mastering the Art of French Cooking, her first book, came out in 1961, when she was 49.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child (too tall at 6 feet 2 for the Women's Army Corps or the WAVES)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child (born August 15, 1912; Mastering the Art of French Cooking, 1961)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child (OSS shark repellent)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child (Dr. Juliet Bleeb in We're Back! A Dinosaur's Story, 1993)

cards.say: The Pig War [started when a British farmer shot an American's pig], [had a pig as its only casualty], [left US and British troops sharing one island for about 12 years], and [was settled by the German Kaiser in 1872].
cards.real: It was the other way around: American Lyman Cutlar shot a pig belonging to Britain's Hudson's Bay Company in June 1859.
src: https://home.nps.gov/sajh/learn/historyculture/the-pig-war.htm/index.htm
https://home.nps.gov/sajh/learn/historyculture/the-pig-war.htm/index.htm

https://home.nps.gov/sajh/learn/historyculture/the-pig-war.htm/index.htm

cards.say: The Hope Diamond [was stolen with the French crown jewels in 1792], [keeps glowing red after an ultraviolet light is switched off], [was dug out of a South African mine in the 1800s], and [was sent to the Smithsonian by registered mail in a brown paper box].
cards.real: It came from the Kollur Mine in India. The gem trader Tavernier bought it there in 1666 and sold it to Louis XIV of France.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Diamond (stolen in 1792 with most of the crown jewels)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Diamond (intense red phosphorescence after short-wave ultraviolet light)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Diamond (Kollur Mine, India; Tavernier bought it in 1666 and sold it to Louis XIV)
https://postalmuseum.si.edu/collections/object-spotlight/hope-diamond-package; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Diamond (1958, registered mail, brown paper)

cards.say: Big Ben [is the name of the bell, not the clock or the tower], [rings for a clock kept on time with old pennies on its pendulum], [cracked soon after it was hung and went silent for four years], and [hangs in a tower renamed for the Queen's 1953 coronation].
cards.real: The Clock Tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee, her 60th year on the throne.
src: https://www.parliament.uk/about/living-heritage/building/palace/big-ben/facts-figures/ (Big Ben, the Great Bell); https://www.history.com/articles/how-did-big-ben-get-its-name
https://www.parliament.uk/about/living-heritage/building/palace/big-ben/facts-figures/great-clock-facts/ (pre-decimal pennies regulate the clock)
https://www.history.com/articles/how-did-big-ben-get-its-name (first rang July 11, 1859, cracked two months later and fell silent for upwards of four years)
https://www.history.com/articles/how-did-big-ben-get-its-name (renamed Elizabeth Tower for the Diamond Jubilee in 2012); https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/world/109300/big-ben-to-be-renamed-elizabeth-tower
